description:
With Valeri Ponzo. An unexpected trip south from a job in Lakeland via meeting the crew in Tampa at 0530. Val texted me that the Black-billed Cuckoo found yesterday at Pinecraft Park in Sarasota was seen again this morning, and she was going for it when she got off work at noon. She found the cuckoo -- a lifer! -- by 1315 and called me. I headed down from Tampa and Val showed me the cuckoo, which was extremely cooperative, almost immediately. It was a photographic lifer for me; Black-billed Cuckoo is a surprisingly tough bird in Florida; I've seen only three or four in 40+ years of birding the state. The weather at the start was sunny, 83 degrees ("feels like" 87), and breezy. We left at  1558 and headed to Gecko's Grill for dinner. I got home at 2106.

Because I had no optics with me, I used Val's camera to take these images. Val's camera tends to take slightly unfocused photographs more often than focused photographs, for some inexplicable reason. Oh well ... Plus, the lighting was pretty dreadful, so many of my images are intentionally overexposed to show detail in the subjects.

A lifer for Val and a photographic lifer for me!
